300 years later…

SCP-4444-J's portal was found in a sealed section of the foundation. Inside we found SCP-4444-J-1, records show the former scientist deleted all info of 4444-J in the past, locked himself away with the portal, and remained petrified in a facepalm position for three centuries. Following it's rediscovery, the containment team became SCP's 4444-J-2 through 18, in similar states to SCP-4444-J-1.

item.title: Re: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Ok, so, dear god is this article outdated. It should either be updated to contain references to all those other, newer fan sites (which is a bit mean-spirited), relegated outside of the -J main list (-J-ARC anyone?) or just deleted. This article paints a really bad picture of the site for newbies, and for many acts as a model of behaviour when interacting with fan sites. It's nice to make fun and all, but we really shouldn't be promoted this kind of mean-spirited dogpiling on the main site. I really don't like having this one on the -J list, as its fancy number and name draws a whole bunch of clicks, and paints a pretty bad picture of what our -J standards are.

Anyways, regardless of what message this article is sending, the main article itself is not very funny at all (only the supplement page really brings it any humor at all aside from the jabbing in this article), and as per usually site policy it's generally good practice to vote based on the quality of the article itself, not just the supplements. I think the site would be perfectly fine if we just downvoted this one into oblivion and then relegated the supplement page to tale status.
